title: Context clues
lede: Most new words come with hints sitting right next to them. Here's how to read the hints.

sections.md:
## Why context comes first
You'll meet far more words in reading than anyone can teach you one at a time. The skill that scales is figuring out a word from the sentence around it. Five kinds of clue show up again and again.

## The five clue types
| Clue | Signal words | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Definition | is, means, refers to, commas or dashes | A **broker**, someone who arranges deals between others, set up the load. |
| Synonym | or, also, like, in other words | The plan was **feasible**, or doable, with the budget we had. |
| Antonym or contrast | but, however, unlike, instead | Unlike his **gregarious** brother, Sam kept to himself. |
| Example | such as, including, for instance | **Perishable** freight, such as produce and dairy, needs a reefer. |
| General sense | the whole situation | After three missed payments, the lender **repossessed** the truck. |

sections.title: Using a contrast clue
sections.problem: "The first offer was **paltry**, but the second was generous enough to accept."
steps: Spot the signal: **but** means the next idea contrasts.
So the first was the opposite: small, not enough.

sections.md:
## The method
1. Stop at the word. Don't skip it.
2. Find the signal word, if there is one.
3. Guess a simple replacement word.
4. Plug your guess into the sentence. If it reads naturally, you're close.
5. Check a dictionary later if the word matters.

sections.label: Context has limits
sections.md: Sometimes the sentence gives no real clue. When the word matters (a contract, a test question), look it up. Context gets you the gist; a dictionary gets you the exact meaning.

practice.q: "The mechanic gave a **cursory** look at the engine, glancing at it for only a few seconds." Cursory means…
practice.why: "Only a few seconds" is a definition clue.

practice.q: "Unlike the **frugal** owner, his partner spent money on everything." Frugal means…
practice.why: "Unlike" signals contrast with spending on everything.

practice.q: "**Arid** regions, such as deserts and dry plains, get little rain." Arid means…
practice.why: Example clue: deserts and dry plains.

practice.q: "The new rule was **ambiguous**; even the managers couldn't agree on what it meant." Ambiguous means…
practice.why: General sense: nobody agreed on the meaning.

practice.q: "She was **adamant**, refusing to change her mind no matter what we said." Adamant means…
practice.why: Definition clue right after the comma.

practice.q: "The tiny cafe was **unassuming**, but the food was the best in the city." Unassuming means…
practice.why: "But" contrasts a plain place with excellent food.
